headlines.text: On this day in 2024, it was title-change night for the AEW World Heavyweight Title as Jon Moxley vs. Bryan Danielson battled it out, appearing on WrestleDream, rated 8.59 ? an incredible outing ? ending the champion's reign at 3 defenses. In a match that also ended Bryan Danielson's full-time in-ring career, Moxley choked him unconscious with the Bulldog Choke to become a four-time AEW World Champion, with the Death Riders finishing the beatdown by pulling a plastic bag over his head.

That Wednesday in 2022, the AEW All-Atlantic Title changed hands as Orange Cassidy vs. PAC battled it out, appearing on Dynamite, rated 7.86 ? a well-paced, entertaining battle ? ending the champion's reign at 4 defenses. PAC reached for a ring-bell hammer but was foiled by Danhausen's interference, letting Cassidy land back-to-back Orange Punches to finally beat PAC and win his first AEW singles title.

2024 brought us this moment: the AEW International Title changed hands as Konosuke Takeshita vs. Ricochet vs. Will Ospreay battled it out, appearing on WrestleDream, rated 9.13 ? an outstanding performance from both sides ? ending the champion's reign at 3 defenses. Fletcher's screwdriver stab to Ospreay's head set up Takeshita's knee strike to win the AEW International Championship, ending Ospreay's second reign at 48 days.

secondaries.text: Looking back to 2024, when Jay White vs. Adam Page delivered a fantastic contest on WrestleDream, rated 8.14, on an outstanding WrestleDream '24 show that earned an overall rating of 8.48.
Turning the clock back to 2022: Chris Jericho vs. Bryan Danielson fought tooth and nail for the ROH World Heavyweight Title, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.77.
Turning the clock back to 2024: Mariah May vs. Willow Nightingale fought tooth and nail for the AEW Women's World Title, appearing on WrestleDream, rated 7.34 ? a well-paced, entertaining battle.
